title: Barcode vs Manual Logging: What Actually Keeps Beginners Tracking
summary:
Most people don't quit calorie tracking because they don't care about their health. They quit because logging a meal feels like homework. I learned this building CalyFit, a free calorie tracker aimed at beginners and busy people — and the barcode scanner versus manual entry debate turned out to be less about technology and more about friction.

Here is the honest version of what works, what doesn't, and how to design logging so people actually stick with it.

The real enemy is friction, not willpower

A beginner opening a calorie app for the first time faces two questions: "What did I just eat?" and "How much effort will it take to record it?" If the second answer is "a lot," the first question stops mattering. People skip the entry, then skip the day, then quietly delete the app.

title: AI vs Human WordPress Writing
summary:
A comparison of AI writing tools and human writers for WordPress content.

Should we embrace AI for content creation or stick with human writers? After extensive testing with both approaches, below is what I found.

The Reality of AI Writing Tools

AI writing has evolved beyond the keyword-stuffing bots of yesterday. Modern tools like Claude and GPT-4 produce grammatically correct, coherent content that reads naturally. They excel at technical documentation, code generation, and scaling content production. What takes human writers hours happens in minutes.

Yet AI tools struggle with nuanced understanding from real-world experience. When we write about debugging WordPress plugin conflicts at 2 AM or handling client scope creep, that authenticity resonates. AI describes these scenarios without living them. The consistency of AI output becomes both strength and weakness, plateauing at “good enough” for most use cases.

summary:

The die function ends your Perl program with an error string, and you'll often see code like: die "My error" unless $i > 5 or die "Other error" if check(), because Perl just loves the backwards conditionals. What's even more fun with die is how it behaves with eval blocks, so it doesn't always kill your program, sometimes it is how you pass error strings back out of sections of your program.
